title: Edit sudo configuration safely
summary: Use visudo to edit the sudoers file. This prevents syntax errors that could lock you out of sudo access.

steps.explain: Open the main sudoers file with visudo. It checks for syntax errors before saving.

rollback.explain: If you made a mistake and cannot save, exit without saving (usually Ctrl+C or :q! in vi). If you saved a bad config, you may need to boot into recovery mode to fix it.

warnings: Never edit /etc/sudoers with a standard text editor like nano or vim directly without visudo. A syntax error will break sudo for all users.
If you are using a drop-in file in /etc/sudoers.d/, use 'sudo visudo -f /etc/sudoers.d/filename'.
